title: Multidimensional Insight Stacking
opening: Keep each method beside the examples that produced its finding. Repeated wording can share one origin, and different findings can both matter.

labels.sourceExcerpt: Multidimensional Insight Stacking compares the methods themselves. Sort candidate values into repeated, context-specific and surprising or conflicting findings. Investigate the differences before merging them into a single account.

example.title: Example: Two findings, two contexts
example.first: A journal review suggests solitude supports concentrated creation.
example.second: A review of meaningful memories suggests shared work supports learning from others.
example.account: The examples suggest both preferences may matter under different conditions. They do not establish one permanent identity or that these are independent sources.
example.action: Compare a recent solo project with a collaborative one. Record what the task required and what you preferred in each.

source.assessmentBoundary: Open-ended answers have no stored gold answer. Syntactic validity does not establish understanding, transfer or outcome success.
source.distinctions: Page 40 describes comparing methods, sorting candidate values as repeated, context-specific or surprising/conflicting, investigating differences, then merging into an account. The practice keeps original examples and shared origin visible so merging does not erase evidence or treat reused material as independent.
source.limits: The supplied manuscript is the source; authorship or adoption of every wording is not independently established. The solitude/shared-work scenario is an authored illustration, not observed learner data. Private practice here does not establish independent learner effectiveness or author acceptance.
